facts.raw_span: A woman in her 50s
morbid obesity and obstructive sleep apnea
3 days of fever with a temperature up to 39°C
anosmia
shortness of breath
Oxygen saturation of 85% on room air
coarse rales at the lung bases bilaterally
Nasopharyngeal swab positive by reverse transcriptase–polymerase chain reaction
Chest Radiography: Suggestive of bilateral multifocal pneumonia
Normal sinus rhythm with normal frontal QRS axis
Precordial leads showed low amplitudes and Q waves in leads V1 to V3
Normal ECG findings

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms, including fever, anosmia, and shortness of breath, along with the positive nasopharyngeal swab and chest radiography suggestive of bilateral multifocal pneumonia, are consistent with COVID-19.

The patient's symptoms, including fever, shortness of breath, and coarse rales at the lung bases bilaterally, along with the chest radiography suggestive of bilateral multifocal pneumonia, are consistent with community-acquired pneumonia.

The patient's symptoms, including fever, anosmia, and shortness of breath, are consistent with influenza, although the positive nasopharyngeal swab and chest radiography are more suggestive of COVID-19.

The patient's symptoms, including shortness of breath, coarse rales at the lung bases bilaterally, and chest radiography suggestive of bilateral multifocal pneumonia, are consistent with pneumococcal pneumonia.
The patient's history of obstructive sleep apnea and symptoms, including shortness of breath and coarse rales at the lung bases bilaterally, may be related to an increased risk of pneumonia.
